problem: On iPhone Safari, pricing/lifecycle and monthly/yearly controls rendered but taps produced no state change. The language selector showed 'Switching language failed. Try again.' and the page remained Dutch.
root_cause: Pricing bound click handlers directly to the initial button nodes. The shared mobile shell can replace/recompose DOM after those handlers are attached, leaving visible replacement buttons without listeners.

The language runtime redirected canonical unprefixed pages to /en/<route>. Release builds deliberately set STATIC_I18N_NETWORK=0, so when the static translation cache is incomplete the English route is not emitted at all. The selector therefore navigated to a route that could be absent.
fix: Move pricing state handling to an external cache-busted runtime with document-level delegated click/change/input handlers.
Switch canonical unprefixed public pages between NL and EN in place using the existing runtime translation endpoint and persisted bg_locale state.
Keep static /nl and /en routes supported when present, but never require them for the interactive language toggle.
Cache-bust i18n.js from the site-wide injector.
prevention: Interactive public controls that survive shell recomposition must use delegated event ownership or be rebound after replacement.
A user-facing language switch may not depend on a build artifact that offline release policy can legally omit.
Browser regression must click affected controls on mobile and verify DOM state changes, not merely verify that buttons render.

evidence.production_before: /prijzen rendered all lifecycle panels and exposed a language-switch failure message
